SATOM 3.0.0

SATOM stops reading Fortinet's website itself and gets its vendor knowledge from signed knowledge packs, warns when a FortiWeb's signature database goes stale, and adds a read-only FortiGate workspace.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user

Released: 2026-10-08 · All releases

In short#

SATOM 3.0 changes where its vendor knowledge comes from. Release notes, the Scout advisory and upgrade paths no longer depend on SATOM reading Fortinet's documentation website: they come from signed knowledge packs that SATOM can fetch every day by itself, or that you upload on an air-gapped node. The release also watches the age of each FortiWeb's signature database and opens a new, read-only FortiGate workspace. Administrators will notice the new Knowledge packs card and the stricter pack signing rules; everyone will see a "Knowledge from…" freshness line on release notes, Scout and the Migration Report.

This is a major version because of one breaking change: packs published from 3.0 on use a new format that older SATOM versions refuse. Read Before you upgrade.

What's new#

Knowledge packs on the Software Update page#

Under Software Update → Knowledge packs you now see, for each kind of pack, which one is installed, its date and its age:

  • the API pack, which is tied to the SATOM release you run;
  • the rolling knowledge pack, which is refreshed independently of releases.

A stale badge appears once a pack is more than 30 days old, and the card shows what the knowledge feed currently offers. Three buttons do the work:

  • Check now asks the feed what is available.
  • Download fetches the pack. Its size and checksum must match what the feed announced; if they do not, nothing is kept.
  • Import loads the pack as a background job. The pack's signature is checked during the import. Import runs on the primary node only.

The card also gives a manual-download link and explains the air-gapped path: download the pack elsewhere and upload it under the API library packs. See Knowledge packs.

A daily knowledge fetch#

A new scheduled action, knowledge fetch, runs once a day. A setting decides how far it goes:

  • off — do nothing;
  • notify — only tell you a newer pack exists;
  • download — download it, but leave the import to you;
  • download and import — the default: download and import it.

By default it reads the public SATOM knowledge feed, but you can point it at any HTTPS mirror. It uses the same connection settings, proxy and certificate checking as the software-update feed. A standby node does nothing and says why. The result of the last run (status, message, time and pack) is kept so you can see what happened. The operator CLI gains matching commands to show the installed knowledge and to fetch a pack by hand (a check first; nothing is downloaded until you confirm). See Scheduled actions and Operator CLI.

"Knowledge from…" on the pages that use it#

The Release Notes window, the Scout advisory and the Migration Report now show which pack their knowledge came from and its date. You get a warning when that pack is older than 30 days, or when no knowledge pack was ever imported, so you know how much to trust the advice.

Signature database freshness for FortiWeb#

  • A new daily scheduled action, signature check, reads only the signature database version of each FortiWeb and records when it last changed. It refreshes SATOM's cached signature catalog only when a version actually changed.
  • The alert engine raises a device alert when a FortiWeb's signature database is older than a set number of days (7 by default), has never been updated, or cannot be read.
  • Administrator → Signatures lists the signature database state per device.
  • When a knowledge pack carries it, signature search and signature details also show public FortiGuard information: the signature name, its severity, the CVEs it covers and a link.

See Signature database freshness.

Richer knowledge packs#

Knowledge packs can now carry more kinds of content. Each item is checked on its own: a malformed item is rejected with its reason, and the rest of the pack still imports. A section your SATOM does not know yet is skipped with a visible warning instead of failing the import.

  • Predefined protection profiles go into the factory catalog, never over a profile SATOM captured from one of your own appliances.
  • Field rename suggestions are shown with a badge. They are never applied for you and never replace a field mapping you made.
  • Baselines are stored for a firmware build that has no baseline of your own, and are never made the active baseline.
  • Signature information (the public FortiGuard details mentioned above).

Every imported row now records where it came from: local, the API pack or a knowledge pack, with the pack's name. You see this origin when you inspect a row, in the pack list, in the import history and in the API pack section of Software Update.

Corrections now reach you#

When a pack wrote something earlier — release notes for a version, the field list of an object, other reference rows — and a newer pack carries a different version of it, the newer one now replaces it. The rules are simple: your own local data always wins and is never replaced; between two packs, the one built from the newer snapshot wins. Data that a 2.x SATOM imported from a pack is recognised as pack data, so it can be corrected too.

The 3.0 API pack replaces the 2.x release packs: a shipped pack whose content an imported pack already carries is no longer reported as pending.

FortiGate workspace (read-only)#

SATOM now has a sixth workspace, for FortiGate. You register a FortiGate with a REST API administrator token in the password field, because FortiOS 8.0 no longer accepts a password on its REST API.

  • A dashboard with a device picker and the live status of the unit.
  • 30 read-only pages in 7 areas that follow the FortiOS 8.0 menu.
  • SATOM only reads: it never sends a change to the FortiGate.
  • When the FortiGate refuses a request, you see an error, never an empty table. An "unauthorised" answer names the usual cause: an unlicensed virtual machine.
  • Secret fields and encrypted values are removed before a row is displayed.
  • Tables stop at 500 rows and say when they were cut.
  • The shared Fleet and Administration pages, the Release Notes window, Build compatibility and Schema builds are reachable from its sidebar.

Not available yet: changes, an API console, backups, firmware and binding to the endpoint registry. See FortiGate workspace.

What changes for you#

  • SATOM no longer reads Fortinet's documentation website. The Scan from Fortinet panel on the release notes pages is gone. Release notes, the Scout advisory and upgrade paths read only what signed packs imported. Collecting from the vendor's website is now done by a separate tool that builds the packs. See The Knowledge Harvester.
  • One key, one use. Each signing key now serves one purpose only. Software update packages are checked only against the update keys; a new-format pack only against the keys for its own kind (API pack or knowledge pack). A pack signed with the wrong kind of key is refused. Keys you add on the node for packs must belong to the system administrator account, or they are refused.
  • The public keys for both kinds of pack ship with SATOM, so the shipped pack imports on a fresh installation and on the first update from 2.x without you installing a key first.
  • Adding a trusted key from the operator CLI now asks for its purpose (update, API pack or knowledge; update by default) and refuses a key that is already trusted for another purpose. Listing the trust store shows the keys grouped by purpose, with their fingerprints. See Pack trust and signing keys.
  • Two new daily scheduled actions exist: knowledge fetch and signature check.
  • The old way of exporting a pack in the 2.x format is still there for local and offline use, but it is marked as legacy and releases no longer use it.

Fixed#

  • In the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator workspaces, the Schema builds and Build compatibility links that appeared in the sidebar since 2.13.0 opened a refusal page. They now open.

Before you upgrade#

  • New pack format. Packs published from 3.0 on use a new format. SATOM 2.13 and older refuse them with an "unsupported pack schema" error, so update SATOM before importing a 3.0-era pack. SATOM 3.0 still imports the older 2.x packs.
  • Version requirement in packs. A pack can name the minimum SATOM version it needs. If it is newer than the SATOM you run, the whole pack is refused and the message tells you which version is needed.
  • Add the two new scheduled actions. On an existing node, run the operator CLI's seed command (satom execute seed actions --yes) so the daily knowledge fetch and signature check are created.
  • Check the fetch mode on online nodes. The default downloads and imports knowledge packs automatically every day. Set it to notify or off if you want to approve each pack yourself. Air-gapped nodes keep uploading packs by hand.
  • After the upgrade, check the trust store and the installed knowledge from the operator CLI. The full procedure, including rollback, is in Upgrading to SATOM 3.0.

Under the hood#

  • An automatic check keeps any part of the application from contacting a Fortinet website again.
  • Each pack records who published it, what it was built from and a fingerprint of its content, which is what allows the "newer snapshot wins" correction rule.
  • Signature metadata from FortiGuard is supported but ships empty for now, because FortiGuard's terms do not allow redistributing it.
